options: Every login on a SQL Server instance, both Windows and SQL authentication, with properties like IsDisabled and PasswordExpirationEnabled
Only currently connected sessions
A list of every table's row counts
Backup history for the instance
questions.explain: Get-DbaLogin enumerates logins and their properties — the starting point for any security audit.

questions.q: What does Test-DbaLoginPassword check by default?
options: Whether a SQL login has an empty password or a password matching the login name itself, using PWDCOMPARE()
Whether the login has ever failed to connect
Whether the login uses Windows Authentication
The login's last password change date only
questions.explain: By default it tests for empty passwords and passwords equal to the username, comparing against password hashes in sys.sql_logins via PWDCOMPARE().

questions.q: What is an orphaned database user, per Get-DbaDbOrphanUser?
options: A database user with no matching server login, often left behind after a dropped login or a restore to a different server
A user account that has been disabled
A login with administrator rights
A user with an expired password
questions.explain: Orphaned users lack a matching login, which can leave permissions attached to an account nobody currently owns or manages.

questions.q: What dbatools cmdlet can remap a reviewed orphaned user to an existing login?
options: Repair-DbaDbOrphanUser
Set-DbaLogin
Copy-DbaLogin
Fix-DbaOrphanUser
questions.explain: Repair-DbaDbOrphanUser follows the Verb-DbaNoun convention and fixes orphaned users by remapping them to a login.

questions.q: What pattern does the lesson's combined audit report reuse from the earlier health-check lesson?
options: Run individual checks, build one structured record, and only surface/email it when something actually needs attention
Run every check every second in an infinite loop
Email the full raw output of every cmdlet regardless of findings
Disable all logins automatically if any issue is found
questions.explain: Both lessons follow the same principle: filter to real signal and only alert when something is actually wrong.
